newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: At least 33 die in Colombia bus crash.
newsitem.headline: At least 33 die in Colombia bus crash.

text.p: At least 33 people died and three were injured when a bus plunged into a 1,500-foot (500 metres) deep ravine in the Andes mountains of southwest Colombia on Friday, Red Cross officials said.
Rescue workers struggled to reach the wrecked bus at the bottom of the ravine. By Friday afternoon they had rescued only three injured passengers and recovered three bodies.

The accident occurred near the town of Ricaurte, in Narino province on Colombia's southern border with Ecuador. Police said the bus, which was travelling from Cali, Colombia's second largest city, to the small Pacific coast port of Tumaco, was thought to have been carrying 36 passengers.

"We have rescued three injured and retrieved three corpses so far. Rescuers say there are no other signs of life down in the ravine and say all the other bus occupants died," said Henry Palacios, head of the Red Cross in the provincial capital Pasto.

Narino police chief Fortunato Guanarita said the bus was completely destroyed in the plunge and the cause of the accident was not immediately known. A combination of treacherous highways and poorly maintained buses are the most frequently cited causes of accidents.
It is the second fatal bus accident in Narino in the last 10 days. Fifteen people died and 18 were injured when a local bus fell into a 900-foot (300 metres) ravine on Dec. 23.
